prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your neighborhood, budget, timing, and what matters most (lowest price, longest warranty, fastest service, brand preference, etc.). A few quick questions will let me give a tailored short list and sample bids to request:

- What Atlanta ZIP code or neighborhood are you in?
- Do you have a preferred brand (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Rheem, Goodman, etc.)?
- Rough budget or target SEER (efficiency) level?
- Do you need the job done urgently (next few days) or can you wait for bids?

While you answer, here’s a practical plan and what to look for when choosing an AC contractor in Atlanta.

How to choose the best company
1. Get 3 written bids that are apples-to-apples:
   - Same capacity (tons) and SEER rating
   - Matched indoor coil and proper refrigerant
   - Include permits, removal/disposal of old unit, and labor warranty
   - Show line-set, electrical, and any ductwork or thermostat work separately

2. Require a proper load calculation (Manual J) and equipment selection (Manual S) — not just “replace like for like.” This ensures the right size and efficiency.

3. Verify credentials:
   - Georgia business license and local permits for Atlanta (City of Atlanta or county)
   - Proof of insurance (liability and workers’ comp)
   - NATE-certified technicians is a plus
   - Manufacturer dealer status for warranties (e.g., authorized Carrier/Trane dealer)

4. Compare warranties:
   - Manufacturer warranty (parts and compressor) and labor warranty
   - Ask what voids the warranty (improper installation, no annual maintenance, etc.)

5. Check reputation:
   - Google Reviews, Yelp, BBB, Angi/HomeAdvisor
   - Ask for recent local references and photos of similar installs

6. Ask about specifics:
   - Will indoor coil and refrigerant match and be vacuumed and leak-tested?
   - Ductwork inspection and recommendations
   - Thermostat included (smart thermostat?)
   - Estimated timeline and cleanup/disposal

Typical price range (Atlanta, ballpark)
- Central AC full replacement (complete outdoor condenser + indoor coil + labor): roughly $4,000–$12,000.
- Factors: unit brand and SEER, complexity of install, ductwork repairs, electrical upgrades.
(Price ranges are approximate — get local bids.)

Red flags
- Very low price with no written details
- Refusal to perform Manual J load calc
- Push to replace with an oversized unit
- No proof of insurance or license
- High-pressure “today only” sales tactics

Companies that commonly operate in Atlanta
(These are well-known regional/national names you can consider when getting quotes — I can build a local shortlist for your ZIP)
- Coolray & Mr. Plumber
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (ARS)
- One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin (local franchises)
- Service Experts (local branch)
- Local independent contractors with strong Google/Yelp reviews — often provide competitive prices and personalized service

If you want, I can:
- Provide a 3-company shortlist for your ZIP code
- Draft a phone script or email template you can use to request bids and compare quotes
- Create a simple comparison checklist you can fill in from each estimate

Tell me your ZIP code and any preferences and I’ll find a short list and a ready-to-use checklist.
